substantive_reconstruction.factorization_and_character: For orthogonal Schur-Weyl projectors, wλ=tr(Pλρ^⊗n)≥0 and Σλwλ=1. It factorizes as fλ times the Schur-character trace on the unitary irrep, not the trace of an arbitrary nonorthogonal Young symmetrizer. Put p=λ/n, h=d(d−1)/2 and Cλ=n!/∏λ_i!. In a semistandard tableau character, the row-constant tableau contributes s^λ; content ν satisfies ν↓≺λ by the column-capacity condition. Rearrangement and summation by parts against decreasing log s give s^ν≤s^λ, so s^λ≤character≤mλs^λ. No converse asserting survival of every filling is required.
substantive_reconstruction.finite_bounds: Row-assignment counting gives fλ≤Cλ. The padded hook formula fλ=n!∏_{i<j}(λ_i−λ_j+j−i)/∏_i(λ_i+d−i)! gives fλ≥Cλ/(n+d)^h: the numerator factors are at least one and the h extra denominator factors are at most n+d. Weyl's formula gives mλ≤(n+d)^h. Also (n+1)^−d exp(nH(p))≤Cλ≤exp(nH(p)). For the lower bound, the multinomial type λ is a mode at parameter p=λ/n: each coordinate factorial ratio for an increase or decrease is ≤1, with zero-probability coordinates handled separately. At most (n+1)^d types sum to one. Combining these inequalities proves (n+d)^−(h+d)e^−nD≤wλ≤(n+d)^h e^−nD.
substantive_reconstruction.zero_support_and_rate: If rank ρ=q and λ has more than q rows, its first column cannot be strictly filled by q positive-weight labels, so the character and weight vanish and D=∞. Otherwise the supported character proof applies with zero components omitted, and gives the same padded bounds. For supported nonzero blocks, −log(wλ)/n=D(p||s)+O_d(log(n+d)/n). The bare bound is false: s=(1/2,1/2), n=2, λ=(2,0) has wλ=3/4 but exp(−nD)=1/4.
substantive_reconstruction.concentration: For fixed ε, the supported closed ε-away set has positive KL minimum δ_ε unless empty. Counting at most (n+1)^d diagrams yields outside mass ≤(n+1)^d(n+d)^h exp(−nδ_ε)→0. This proves total neighborhood concentration, not positive constant mass for each nearby atom or exact finite-grid equality.
